name: Hour IV — The Road Gives Way

tokens.text: -1. If Dissonance is in the Glitch band or higher, -2 instead.
-2. If you fail, raise Dissonance by 1.
-3. If the Appointed is Sensed or later, take 1 horror.
-4. If you fail, advance the Hourglass by 1 Hour.

name: The Square
text: Every loop begins here. Travel between districts along a connection costs 1 Hour (a Skip).
flavor: Everyone is out for the occultation. None of them will look at you twice — not this time, not ever.

name: The First Hour
text:
Objective — Once 5 clues have been gathered in total, an investigator at the Almanac Steps may resolve the Occultation (no test). When they do, read "The First Reset" (the objective was completed).
If the Hourglass reaches Hour IX first, read "The First Reset" anyway.
flavor: The almanac promised the occultation at midnight. It is eleven, and the sky is already wrong.

name: The First Reset
text:
Each investigator gains 2 banked Memory. If the objective was completed, gain 1 more banked Memory.
Record "You Are Unstuck" in the campaign log. Act I begins.
No Years are gained from the Prologue. Proceed to the first interlude, then Loop 1.
flavor: The occultation completes. Something reaches through — and does not finish reaching. The night folds. You are standing in the Square again at eleven o'clock, salt on your tongue, and you are the only ones who feel the seam.

name: Light the Lamp
text:
Objective — Once 4 clues have been discovered in the Lighthouse district, an investigator at the Lantern Room may test [com] or [wil] (3) to light the lamp. If they succeed, record "The Lamp Was Never Lit."
While the lamp is lit this loop, Echoes at connected districts stay Sleepwalking one band longer. For all future loops, the Lantern Room flips to its calmer side.
flavor: The lamp is dark. It has never, in any loop, been lit.

name: Why Thirteen?
text:
Objective — Once 6 clues have been discovered in the Drowned Church, an investigator at the Vestry may read the register. Record "The Thirteenth Toll."
Hour III no longer adds the Church's extra Dissonance.
flavor: The bell tolled thirteen times at the first occultation. It should toll twelve.

name: The Hour Was Wrong
text:
Act II only, once the log shows "The Thirteenth Toll." The Flooded Crypt opens; the Bell-Ringer Beneath spawns there.
Objective — Recover the drowned almanac-page (3 clues in the Flooded Crypt). Record "The Hour Was Wrong."
Remove Hour IV from the Occultation for all future loops.

name: Walk It Backward
text:
Objective — Move through all three locations in reverse of the Echoes' direction (the Turning, then the Low Bridge, then the Milestones), discovering at least 1 clue at each. Record "The Road Remembers."
Once per loop, travel to or from the Lighthouse via the Sunken Road costs 0 Hours.
flavor: The same figures walk it every loop, in the same direction, never arriving.

name: Who Walks Beside You
text:
Act II only, once the log shows "The Road Remembers."
Objective — At the Turning, evade or Hold an awakened Echo and read the face beneath the hood. Record "Who Walks Beside You."
Echoes get -1 fight against investigators who have this fact.
flavor: Some of them turn to look at you now.

name: The Sheriff Is Already Dead
text:
Objective — Once 5 clues have been discovered in the Square district, an investigator at the Well may examine the body. Record "The Sheriff Is Already Dead."
From now on, once per loop, an investigator at the Town Hall Steps may look at the top card of the Occultation.
flavor: He has been dead since ten o'clock. No one has noticed but you.

name: The Vote That Never Ends
text:
Act II only, once the log shows "The Sheriff Is Already Dead." When this objective is attempted, What Wears the Sheriff spawns at the Records Office.
Objective — Find the ledger in the Records Office (3 clues there). Record "The Vote That Never Ends" and advance Seraphine's thread, "Who Opened the Door."
flavor: Ending the loop cleanly requires a cost the town agreed to pay.

name: The Wheel Still Turns
text:
Objective — An investigator at the Wheel may test [agi] (3) to ride it. If they succeed, they discover 2 clues from a height (from any location in the Fairground). Record "The Wheel Still Turns."
Once per loop, from the Wheel, you may look at the top 2 encounter cards and reorder them.
flavor: You see the whole town at once.

name: The Ticket-Taker's Bargain
text:
Act II only, once the log shows "The Wheel Still Turns."
Objective — An investigator at the Ticket Booth may speak with the ticket-taker. He offers a way to end the night that is not free. Record "The Ticket-Taker's Bargain" and mark on the log that the bargain was heard.
flavor: He smiles at you like he's been expecting you for a very long time.

name: What the Almanac Hid
text:
Objective — Once 6 clues have been discovered in the Almanac House, an investigator at the Press may set it to reprint the true occultation time. Record "What the Almanac Hid."
At Hour VI, investigators remove a Static token instead of adding one.
flavor: Where the wrong almanac was printed.

name: The Appointed's Name
text:
Act II only, once the log shows "What the Almanac Hid" and "The Vote That Never Ends." The Sealed Study opens.
Objective — Recover the name inside the Sealed Study (3 clues there). Record "The Appointed's Name"; this completes "Who Opened the Door." The Appointed now arrives exhausted at Hour VII.
Once you know "The Appointed's Name," "The Vote That Never Ends," and any one other deep fact, record "The Way the Night Breaks." The finale may now be attempted.
flavor: Inside is the name the town spoke to call the thing through.

name: Contest the Crossing
text:
Only once the log shows "The Way the Night Breaks": declared at the Sealed Study, or when the Hourglass reaches Hour IX. The Appointed's Approach advances to Arrived; it manifests at the location farthest from the investigators if not already on the board. Dissonance does not reset.
Objective — Before the Hourglass reaches Hour IX, gain contest progress equal to 4 × the number of investigators (12 at three players) by Holding Back the Appointed, spending Knowledge, and reaching the Study. Each Hold Back success and each deep fact spent adds 1.
When the finale ends, read the first resolution that qualifies, R1 to R6.
flavor: An appointment made in ink and never kept. All that's left is to keep it.

name: Take Its Place
text:
Contest reached and an Ancient investigator is present.
One Ancient becomes the night's new anchor — kept behind, decades older, so the loop ends for everyone else. The town wakes for the first time in a hundred years.
Softened if "Who Walks Beside You" is known.

name: Close the Door
text:
Contest reached and you know "The Vote That Never Ends" and "The Appointed's Name."
You pay the price the town agreed to and never paid: everyone present ages +3 Years at once, and the door closes. The cleanest true ending — bought with years.

name: Break Through
text:
Contest reached and "The Keeper's Ninth Death" is known.
You force the night open and all survivors escape — but the loop is only paused. Was it really ended?

name: Seal by Force
text:
Contest reached.
The door is sealed but not closed; one investigator (chosen) ages out doing it.

name: Next Time
text:
Contest not reached, but banked Memory is 12 or more.
The loop wins tonight — but you wake at First Dark closer than ever. Begin a new loop; the finale may be re-attempted.

name: The Loop Wins
text:
Contest not reached and banked Memory is below 12.
The night takes you. The campaign ends.
flavor: The town keeps repeating — and somewhere on the Sunken Road, walking the same direction and never arriving, there are new faces beneath the hoods.

name: The Shape of the Hour
text:
Read at the interlude when Act II begins (3 or more surface facts known, or after Loop 3).
The town has begun to notice that you notice. Somewhere past the edge of the Square, something that has been waiting politely decides to stop waiting.
From the next loop: deep objectives open and the Appointed's Whispers join the encounter deck.

name: The Last Hour
text: You know the shape of the night now. You know what it costs to end it. The only question left is who pays.
flavor: You have lived this night more times than you can hold.
